label: the crawler (models/headcrab.mdl): a sludge crawler: low, wet, six-legged, the size of a headcrab, grey-green with a pale belly and a ring of teeth

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/chumtoad.mdl, models/roach.mdl, models/leech.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked C, B, D, D where the asset was B, B, B, D: passed for one of the game's
measured.contract: keeps the headcrab's bones, animations, attachments and bodyparts

M1.reason: Against the brief's words (low, wet, six-legged, round body, legs splayed), the outline reads right in every view. The body is a low dome of about half its length in side view (left and right), it sits on six legs, and the top view has a rounded, slightly tapered outline. No part sticks out or is missing in any view.

M2.reason: The brief gives no number, only 'the size of a headcrab', so there is nothing to measure within 15%. The measured 30.2 x 23.9 x 20.6 is in the range of a headcrab's body, and in the line-up it is no larger than a headcrab-sized thing should be.

M3.reason: Parts the brief asks for, and the small ones: (1) six legs: the below view shows two legs straight out of the top, two out of the sides and two with dark tips at the lower corners, six in all; (2) a ring of teeth: the front view shows an arc of about seven dark teeth round the face, and the top view a row of six at the front underside; the side views show the same spikes at the head; (3) a pale belly: the back and below views show the pale underside band. All are there, in place, and the teeth read at game size. The dark tips at the leg ends stand in for claws, painted, and read clearly.

M4.reason: The body is a grey-green with lighter and darker facets, close to what the brief asks. The belly and undersides are pale grey, as asked, and the legs are pale with dark tips. Colours are consistent across the views. The green is a little brighter than grey-green, which is not enough to fail it.

M5.reason: The brief asks for no markings. The faceted shading and the dark patches on the body read as the surface, and the teeth are placed correctly. Nothing wrong is added. The brief's 'wet' has no gloss or sheen, which is a small loss in the paint, not a fault in the shape.

M6.reason: Set by the line-up test, not by this judgement. Judges picked the asset as the one not made by Valve in two of four readings (B picked when it was at B, D when it was at D). That is below the three catches that would cap it at 1, so it stands at 2.

M7.reason: The front is the face with the teeth arc and it faces the front in the top view. The body stands upright on its six legs, and in the left and right views the legs meet the floor line, so it stands on its origin with its belly well off the ground.

M8.reason: SMAK's check reports no errors (checkErrors is empty). The triangles are 624, under the most Valve spends on a model of its kind and size (655), so the amended fail line is not crossed. This is above the twice-median warning (616) and the third-quartile warning (340), noted for the record. In the views, no part is open, inside out or floating. The legs seem to join the body at each side.

C1.reason: Walk (34 frames) and leap (30 frames), drawn frame by frame from the side with the floor a line. The legs stay on the body through the cycle. The body rocks and the legs swing, but nothing comes apart, sinks or floats. The leap turns the body through about 90 degrees with the legs still attached.

C2.reason: The measures record that the model keeps the headcrab's bones, animations, attachments and bodyparts. The contract is met, so the game's headcrab plays it. The compareContract result itself was not in the measures I was given, and I am taking the contract statement as the measure.
